plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flower clusters (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. In its native habitat it can grow up to 4 meters tall, and it is now a worldwide symbol of the Christmas season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in warm regions such as Florida, California, Hawaii, and the Mediterranean, and as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts, which change color in response to the long nights of short-day photoperiods. The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used it to make dye and medicine.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like, cup-shaped flowers. It thrives in mild, humid winters and partially shaded locations, and thousands of cultivars have been developed.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, the UK, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and it has been cultivated in Japan for centuries, where it is called tsubaki and symbolizes the arrival of winter's beauty.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tropical tree with fern-like leaves that becomes covered in vivid clusters of flowers. In parts of the Southern Hemisphere, it blooms during the summer months, creating spectacular scarlet canopies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); also blooms in late spring to summer in the tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in northern Australia, Brazil, southern Africa, and tropical regions of the Caribbean and Asia
plants.funFact: This tree is considered critically endangered in its native Madagascar, even though it is one of the most commonly planted ornamental trees in the tropics. Its seed pods can reach 60 cm in length and rattle in the wind.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-shaped leaves and tall, leafless stems topped by large, rounded umbels of trumpet-shaped flowers. It is hardy, drought-tolerant, and a favorite in summer gardens of the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South Africa's Eastern Cape; naturalized and cultivated in Australia, New Zealand, Chile, and coastal California
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true lily. The name Agapanthus comes from the Greek words agape (love) and anthos (flower), and in some regions it has become an invasive weed.
